{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2025}} {{Infobox college sports team season |year=2024–25 |team=Texas Longhorns |sport=Basketball |image=Texas Longhorns logo.svg |conference=Southeastern Conference |short_conf= SEC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record= 19–16 |conf_record= 6–12 |head_coach= [[Rodney Terry]] |hc_year= 2nd |asst_coach1= [[Frank Haith]] |ac1_year = 2nd |asst_coach2 = [[Steve McClain]] |ac2_year = 3rd |asst_coach3 = Brandon Chappell |ac3_year = 3rd |asst_coach4 = Byron Jones |ac4_year = 2nd |asst_coach5 = Nick Matson |ac5_year = 1st |stadium=[[Moody Center]] |champion=[[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]] champions |tourney =[[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = First Four }} {{2024–25 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They played their home games at the [[Moody Center]] in [[Austin, Texas]], as members of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. The Longhorns were led by second-year head coach [[Rodney Terry]]. They finished the season 19–16, 6–12 in SEC play to finish in a tie for 13th place. As the No. 13 seed in the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they defeated [[2024–25 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] and [[2024–25 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] before losing to [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 11 seed in the Midwest region. There they lost to [[2024–25 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] in the First Four. On March 23, 2025, the school fired head coach Rodney Terry.{{Cite web |last=Vertuno |first=Jim |date=2025-03-23 |title=Texas fires coach Rodney Terry after Longhorns make another quick exit from NCAA Tournament |url=https://apnews.com/article/texas-rodney-terry-fired-af0786b3f137fa6d013286911f407029 |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=AP News |language=en}} The next day, the school named [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] head coach [[Sean Miller]] the team's new coach.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-24 |title=Sean Miller hired by Texas: Longhorns move quickly, bring in Xavier coach to replace Rodney Terry |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/sean-miller-hired-by-texas-longhorns-move-quickly-bring-in-xavier-coach-to-replace-rodney-terry/ |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} The season marked the first season for Texas as members of the Southeastern Conference. ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Longhorns]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 21–13, 9–9 in [[2023–24 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 play]] to finish in a tie for seventh place. As the No. 7 seed in the [[2020 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]], they lost [[2023–24 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the second round. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 7 seed in the Midwest region. They defeated [[2023–24 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]] in the first round before losing to [[2023–24 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in the round of 32.
